T2: Floating table

solution.text:
T2: Floating table
a. Equilibrium forces and stability
Treat each pair of chains as one chain with the combined tension. Let \(C\) be the uniform plate's centre of mass, \(A\) the movable short-chain attachment, and \(B\) the movable long-chain attachment. The diagram gives horizontal lever arms \(BC=4a\), \(BA=2a\), short-chain length \(4a\), and long-chain length \(6a\).

\[F_1-F_2-mg=0,\qquad 4amg-2aF_1=0,\qquad F_1=2mg,\quad F_2=mg.\]
Both tensions are positive. To check stability one must also account for the constraints. A small horizontal displacement \(x\) cannot produce first-order rotation: both chain attachments initially move horizontally and rigid-body length constraints make their first-order velocities equal. The tilt and vertical centre displacement are of order \(x^2\). Both chain forces then acquire horizontal components opposite to \(x\).

\[F_x\simeq-F_1\frac{x}{4a}-F_2\frac{x}{6a}=-\frac{2mg}{3a}x.\]
This restoring force proves stable equilibrium, with tension maintained for sufficiently small oscillations.
b. Small-oscillation period
\[\ddot x+\frac{2g}{3a}x=0,\qquad T=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{3a}{2g}}=0.777\,\mathrm s.\]
Alternative: constraint geometry and energy

Let the centre shift by \((x,y)\), and let \(\varphi\) be the small clockwise tilt. To the order needed, short- and long-chain length conservation gives
\[x^2-8a(y-2a\varphi)=0,\qquad x^2+12a(y-4a\varphi)=0.\]
\[y=\frac{x^2}{3a},\qquad\varphi=\frac{5x^2}{48a^2},\qquad U=\frac{mgx^2}{3a},\qquad K\simeq\frac12m\dot x^2.\]
The positive quadratic potential establishes stability independently. Since \(y\) and \(\varphi\) are second order in \(x\), their kinetic-energy contributions are higher order. The energy equation gives the same period.
Alternative: trajectory curvature


At equilibrium the instantaneous angular velocity vanishes and every point has speed \(v\). The centre-path curvature is then linear in horizontal coordinate. At \(B\) it is \(-1/(6a)\), and at \(A\), \(1/(4a)\). Extrapolating from their horizontal positions, \(x_B=4a\), \(x_A=2a\), gives centre curvature \(2/(3a)\), or radius \(R_C=3a/2\). Therefore \(T=2\pi\sqrt{R_C/g}\). Equivalently the normal-acceleration construction gives \(w_C=w_B+2w_{Ay}=v^2/(6a)+2v^2/(4a)=v^2/(3a/2)\). Original construction diagrams and marking details remain in the PDF.
